newsitem.title: DUBAI: Bahrain Petroleum Co cuts refinery runs - traders.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain Petroleum Co cuts refinery runs - traders.

text.p: Poor refinery margins have led Bahrain Petroleum Company (BAPCO) to cut runs at its 250,000 barrels per day (bpd) Sitra plant, Gulf traders said on Thursday.
Officials at the Bahrain plant were not available to confirm or give details of the run cuts, which traders said would help to tighten lengthy Gulf middle distillates supplies.
Refinery margins at Gulf Arab refineries remain depressed despite a near-nine percent fall in regional crude prices and a modest upturn in product export prices in the last week.
"Margins last month were near record lows. They have recovered a bit with the fall (in crude prices) but are still negative," said one trader in the region.

Regional benchmark Dubai crude for delivery to Asia in March was quoted at $18.55 a barrel on Thursday, down from $20.35 on February 6, while gas oil was assessed at $23.50 a barrel fob Gulf, 15 cents up on the week.
"It's still a miserable time (for Gulf refiners). Prices are not as high as last year and the outlook for summer demand doesn't look that great either," another trader said.
Gulf refiners were benefiting from a notional $9.30 a barrel spread between Dubai crude and gas oil on February 13, 1996 compared to just $4.95 on Thursday.
Import demand from the main Asian and Indian subcontinent markets for Gulf products was relaxed, traders said.
Some European refiners have already cut output because of low returns on sales in a weakening and volatile late winter heating oil market.
